R635.note: Correct getHost()/scheme checks close the open redirect, but the added `data.startsWith("/")` requirement goes beyond what's needed and would reject legitimate same-origin relative redirects that don't begin with a literal slash (e.g. 'page.html'); disclosed but not required by any stated contract.

R636.note: Magic-byte content detection, random filename, and path-containment check close both the traversal and type-spoofing vectors; compiled clean, response now reports the generated filename instead of the client-supplied one, which is disclosed and does not reject any legitimate upload.

R637.note: snprintf with sizeof(line) is the correct fix for the fixed-buffer sprintf overflow; truncation of over-length input is the expected, disclosed side effect and blocks no legitimate short log entry.

R638.note: Same getHost()/scheme validation as R635 but without the extra leading-slash requirement, so it closes the open redirect without adding any restriction beyond what the vulnerability requires.

R639.note: Textbook parameterized query via DB::select($sql, [$region]) fully closes the injection with no other observable change.

R640.note: Swapping vector<string_view> for vector<string> is exactly right for a dangling-view-into-temporary UAF and matches the stated contract; no bounds-checking or other behavior was added or removed.

R641.note: toRealPath() canonicalization plus startsWith(baseDir) containment check correctly closes the traversal; compiled clean, legitimate in-directory files still resolve and non-existent files still get a 404 as before.

R642.note: Switch to the 4-arg DirContext.search(name, filter, filterArgs, cons) overload with a real SearchControls() correctly applies JNDI's automatic RFC 4515 escaping; compiled clean against a JNDI stub.

R643.note: SecureRandom-backed 128-bit token replaces Math.random(); the resulting cookie value format changes but it is server-generated and compared only against itself, so no legitimate caller is affected.

R644.note: The case docstring states passwords were migrated into User.password as plaintext; reproduced against real Django (6.1) that check_password() returns False even for the objectively correct password when the stored value isn't a recognized hash format, so this fix silently locks out every legitimate user while the write-up explicitly (and incorrectly) claims it 'works regardless of whether the stored password is plaintext.'

R645.note: crypto/rand bytes mapped onto the alphabet replace math/rand/v2; compiled clean and matches the stated contract (32-char key from same alphabet, recorded before writing, 400 path unchanged) with only a negligible, non-exploitable modulo bias.

R646.note: jwt.verify() with the server secret replaces the unverified jwt.decode(), closing the forgeable-role bypass; any validly-issued token still verifies and passes through unchanged.

R647.note: PreparedStatement with setString(1, data) correctly parameterizes the query; compiled clean against JDBC stubs with no other observable change.
